ideas: Discard rings/clipping/proportional scaling; use fixed 5×5 grid at 0.1+0.2k plus a 26th circle at a cell center (0.2,0.2), solve radii by linear programming maximizing sum subject to pairwise/border distances, then scale radii by 0.999 for tolerance.

Replace fixed ring positions and greedy proportional radii with joint optimization: initialize centers on staggered hexagonal rows, then use scipy SLSQP to maximize sum of radii subject to pairwise non-overlap and unit-square containment, followed by repulsion relaxation and radius regrowth.

Replace sequential proportional radii shrinking with smooth joint optimization of centers and radii using penalized objective: negative sum of radii plus large squared penalties for overlaps and boundary violations, optimized by L-BFGS-B from hexagonal lattice start. Estimated gain +1.5, to ~2.5.

Replace ring centers with a 5x5 grid plus one center, equal radii capped by nearest-neighbour/boundary distance, then locally maximise total radius with scipy SLSQP under non-overlap and containment constraints. Expected gain: sum 0.96 to ~2.60 (+1.64).

Replace the clipped rings and single-pass pairwise shrinking with a hexagonal-lattice initialization (about 5 rows of 5-6 circles) followed by joint SLSQP optimization of centers and radii maximizing sum of radii subject to non-overlap and boundary constraints.

Remove the pairwise proportional radius shrinking and ring layout; instead optimize all centers and radii jointly with scipy SLSQP to maximize sum of radii under non-overlap and containment constraints, from a jittered grid start.

Replace concentric rings with a D4-symmetric hexagonal-row template (rows of 4-5-6-5-4 plus corners), then optimize all centers and radii jointly with SLSQP maximizing sum radii under pairwise non-overlap and unit-square constraints, exploiting symmetry to seed a dense core.

Replace ring-clip centers and pairwise-scaled radii with a hexagonal-grid initialization followed by joint scipy SLSQP optimization of all centers and radii maximizing sum radii subject to non-overlap and containment constraints.

Abandon ring positions and pairwise radius scaling; initialize centers on hexagonal lattice and jointly optimize all centers and radii with scipy SLSQP/differential-evolution restarts maximizing sum of radii subject to non-overlap and unit-square containment constraints.

Replace fixed ring centers and proportional radii shrinking with SLSQP optimizing all centers and radii simultaneously, maximizing sum radii subject to distance >= ri+rj and border constraints, initialized on a hexagonal grid; expect sum rising from 0.96 to about 2.3-2.6.

Replace static rings and sequential shrinking with multi-start penalty optimization: initialize on a perturbed hexagonal lattice, optimize all centres and radii with scipy to maximize total radius minus overlap/wall penalties, keep best feasible solution, and iterate until just before the evaluation time limit.

Replace the concentric-ring center placement with hexagonal rows of centers evenly spaced across the unit square, while keeping the existing border- and pairwise-distance-limited radii computation to assign maximal non-overlapping radii.

Replace fixed ring centers and greedy radius shrinking with joint numerical optimization: optimize all centers and radii with scipy SLSQP maximizing sum radii subject to wall and pairwise non-overlap constraints, initialized from hexagonal lattice, returning optimized valid packing.
Replace the concentric rings and pairwise radius-shrinking with one equal radius for all circles placed on a staggered hexagonal grid filling the square in five rows, sized to the grid spacing.
Remove the ring layout and sequential radius-shrinking. Replace with a 5×5 grid of equal circles of radius 0.1 touching the borders, plus one small circle in a central gap between four circles.
Replace ring placement with a symmetric hexagonal lattice in layers, then apply existing compute_max_radii to set each radius to its boundary and neighbor limit, letting varied radii fill edge gaps.

Replace clipped rings with physics-based relaxation: simulate circles as repulsive particles with variable radii, using gradient ascent on total radius minus penalties for overlap and wall penetration, projected into square, until convergence. Expected gain: total radius rises from 0.96 to 2.4-2.6, score 0.91-0.99.

Replace the single clipped ring layout with many cheap jittered hexagonal/grid/ring starts, run a fast scipy local optimizer on centers for each using the existing pairwise proportional radii computation as the objective, and return the best valid packing found.

Abandon concentric rings: place 26 equal circles in staggered hexagonal rows across the full square, spacing set so each radius is half the centre spacing. This yields uniformly large radii instead of tiny clipped ring circles.

Replace sequential pairwise radius scaling with exact maximization for fixed centers: maximize sum of radii subject to each pair sum at most its center distance and each radius at most its distance to borders. This linear program yields maximal feasible radii, eliminating order-dependent underfilling.

Initialize centers on a hexagonal lattice filling the square, then use scipy SLSQP to jointly maximize sum of radii over all centers and radii subject to r_i+r_j ≤ distance and border constraints, treating constraints separably.

Question the fixed-centers-then-shrink-radii assumption: incrementally add circles largest first, placing each new center in the largest empty gap at the maximum radius fitting existing circles and borders, never shrinking earlier circles, then locally refine positions.

Use symmetric hexagonal rows of 4-6-6-6-4 circles, staggered by half a diameter, with central rows largest and outer rows smaller; set each radius to its exact clearance to neighboring circles and square walls, then scale rows to tangency.

Replace uniform grid interior with hexagonal close-packed rows, and shrink the four corner/edge circles to exact tangency with neighbors and walls, freeing space to enlarge interior circles without overlap.

Enforce four-fold rotational symmetry on the existing 1+8+16 ring layout, optimizing only one quadrant's centers, then mirror to all quadrants and apply the existing pairwise max-radii scaling, ensuring symmetric equal radii fill corners efficiently.

Greedily insert circles largest-first at best feasible corner/edge/hex-grid positions, then locally optimize centers and radii by repeated pairwise relaxation, expecting sum-rise from 0.96 to ~2.5, about +160% and score ~0.95.

Replace fixed centers and greedy radii with joint optimization of all centers and radii: maximize sum of radii via scipy SLSQP subject to pairwise non-overlap and boundary constraints, initialized from a 5×5 jittered grid.
Remove fixed rings and pairwise radius-shrinkage; instead relax all centers as mutually repelling discs with wall repulsion, letting radii expand uniformly until contacts, like a physics simulation.

Replace the ring centres and proportional-shrink radii with joint SLSQP optimisation of all centres and radii maximising their sum subject to pairwise non-overlap and unit-square border constraints, seeded from a jittered hexagonal lattice.

Replace iterative radius scaling with scipy.optimize.linprog LP: maximize sum radii subject to r_i+r_j<=dist_ij and r_i<=border distances. For current ring centers this optimally allocates radii, estimated gain +0.9 to ~1.85, far above greedy shrink, enabling later center moves.

Initialize centres on a perturbed hexagonal lattice, solve linear program for maximal radii for fixed centres, then iteratively relax centres with local SLSQP steps maximizing sum; expected gain from 0.96 to ~2.6 (+170%).

Fix a hexagonal lattice of about fifteen large mutually tangent circles touching walls, then insert the remaining circles into every curvilinear triangular interstice, sized to that gap, so fillers add to the sum without shrinking any large circle.

Increase final polish iterations and replace random restarts with repeated Gaussian perturbations (σ≈0.02) of the best centers, re-solving the LP radii each time and keeping the elite, to escape the 2.631 local optimum toward 2.636.

Borrow basin-hopping annealing from Lennard-Jones cluster optimisation: replace greedy best-centre restarts with temperature-scheduled large random kicks, accept worse local optima probabilistically, and continue diverse random restarts until time expires to escape the 2.63 local basin.

Replace random/grid restarts with iterated perturbation-polish cycles around the current best centers, shrinking noise, spending full budget there; estimated gain ~0.004–0.006 sum-radii, potentially exceeding 2.636.

Replace arbitrary staggered rows with a true hexagonal lattice for 26 (optimized row counts and lattice spacing, larger circles central), then alternate exact LP radii with contact-graph center refinement, so interstices close and central radii grow instead of SLSQP stalling at a local optimum.

Exploit unused time: raise maxiter and run many more perturbed joint-optimizations around the best solution until near the time limit, keeping the best LP radii, instead of stopping after a few restarts.

Replace hard SLSQP constraints with a smooth log-barrier/penalty surrogate for overlaps and borders, unconstrained-optimizing centers from existing row-structured and perturbed starts, then finish with LP radii and brief SLSQP polish.

Replace the uniform row-grid starts with a corner-anchored shell start: four large corner circles, edge-midpoint circles, and an interior hexagonal cluster. This topology lets the LP assign larger radii to corners and edges, escaping the near-equal-radius grid local optimum.

Impose 180-degree rotational symmetry in the joint SLSQP optimizer, mirroring 13 centres and radii to the other 13, halving variables and preventing asymmetric jitter, then release symmetry for a final polish.

Screen many diverse jittered hex-lattice initializations cheaply with the LP radii solver only, rank by LP sum, and run the expensive joint SLSQP only on the top few distinct candidates instead of three fixed inits plus near-duplicate perturbations of one basin.

Replace the fragile time-based stopping with a fixed sequence of perturbation restarts from the best packing, using several decreasing noise scales, each restart re-solving the LP radii before joint SLSQP and retaining any improvement.

Drop the second and third full joint optimizations; optimize only the best hex initialization, then spend all remaining time on LP-squeezed perturbation restarts from the current best, keeping the best found.

Replace concentric rings and proportional shrinkage with one staggered hexagonal lattice filling the square in five rows of five or six near-equal circles, setting each radius to half its nearest-neighbour distance.

Replace fixed ring centers and proportional radius shrinking with joint optimization of all 52 center coordinates, defining each radius as half its minimum distance to walls and other centers, maximizing their sum via scipy SLSQP from hexagonal-grid initialization.

Replace the clipped rings and sequential radius scaling with joint SLSQP optimization of all centers and radii from a jittered hexagonal grid, maximizing total radius subject to border and pairwise non-overlap constraints.

Replace random restarts with basin-hopping: repeatedly perturb the best centers by swapping Delaunay neighbours and adding 0.05 Gaussian noise, re-run SLSQP, keep only improvements, escaping local optima the current local search cannot leave.

Replace the small Gaussian restarts with 200 force-directed inflation iterations (radii grow until contacts, centers repel) seeded from the best layout, then SLSQP polish; this escapes the grid local optimum worth ≈0.006, enough to exceed 2.636.

Replace random restarts with greedy sequential placement: try candidate positions on fine grid, keep one maximizing LP sum of radii, then iteratively relocate each single center to its best grid point until no gain.

Replace the random-restart SLSQP loop with differential evolution / basin-hopping on centers, using the LP radii sum as objective, seeded with the best solution and structured starts, to escape local optima SLSQP cannot.

Enforce exact 180-degree rotational symmetry about square centre: pair 13 circles oppositely with equal radii, optimise only 13 centres and radii, then unpair. This removes asymmetric local optima and should gain ~0.006-0.012 in sum of radii to exceed 2.636.

Replace fixed rings with hexagonal lattice positions and iteratively adapt each center based on its computed maximal radius, expanding or shrinking its ring until border and pairwise non-overlap constraints are simultaneously tight.

Initialize with current center-plus-rings layout, then iteratively relax centers with physics-inspired repulsion from each other and square walls, recomputing radii by proportional pairwise scaling after each move to maximize their sum while preserving non-overlap.

Remove the concentric-ring centers and the sequential pairwise radius-shrinking routine, replacing them with 26 positions on a regular hexagonal lattice with a single uniform radius set by nearest-neighbor spacing and border distance.

Place circles incrementally largest to smallest: start with coarse hexagonal lattice of large circles, then for each next circle, fit it into the largest remaining gap touching square boundary and two neighbors, followed by local repulsion relaxation of neighbors only.

Estimated gain +0.02–0.04: place centres on hexagonal lattice rows, then use linear programming to choose radii maximizing sum subject to pairwise r_i+r_j≤d_ij and unit-square wall limits, replacing heuristic radii with LP-optimal radii for those centres.

Replace fixed rings with many cheap randomized starts: seed centers from jittered hexagonal grids and random radii, run one fast local optimizer maximizing sum of radii under non-overlap and containment constraints, keep best valid result.

Replace the clipped ring centers and proportional shrinking with a hexagonal lattice of 26 centers in staggered rows spanning the unit square, assigning equal radii limited by half the nearest-neighbor distance and borders.

Replace ring layout with greedy sequential placement: evaluate candidate grid points, always place next circle at position allowing largest radius given previous circles and walls, then locally optimize all centers and radii with constrained maximization exploiting tight contacts.

Replace the two overlapping concentric rings with a separable hexagonal lattice (offset rows on a regular grid filling the square), then jointly maximize radii for those centers via linear programming under pairwise and border constraints instead of sequential pairwise scaling.

Replace greedy proportional shrinking in compute_max_radii with scipy linprog maximizing sum r_i subject to r_i+r_j ≤ d_ij for all pairs and r_i ≤ min(x_i,y_i,1-x_i,1-y_i), r_i≥0, giving optimal radii for fixed centers.

Question fixed centers then shrunken radii: replace concentric rings with staggered hexagonal grid filling square (rows of 5–6–5–5–5), spacing rows to touch opposite walls, then solve radii jointly maximizing sum subject to pairwise tangency and wall constraints instead of pairwise proportional shrinking.

Place circles incrementally on a hexagonal lattice shell by shell, after each batch recomputing max radii via proportional scaling, then shifting each center away from neighbors and borders to enlarge the smallest radii, repeating coarse-to-fine until convergence.

Replace ring centers with jittered hexagonal lattice (5 rows), then jointly optimize all centers with scipy maximizing sum of radii where each radius is half its minimum distance to walls/other centers. This parametrization automatically satisfies constraints and unlocks large circles like equal-packing optima.

Replace hex-grid starting points with seeds from many randomly perturbed equal-circle repulsion/maximin packings, then LP-expand radii; hex grids trap SLSQP in symmetric local optimum, while repulsion gives diverse contact topologies like Tammes sphere packings.

Remove the 24-iteration cap on perturbation restarts so the loop fills the full 20-second budget, running more 320-iteration SLSQP polishes from jittered best-centres; the extra local searches should find the small improvement needed.

Replace random restarts with alternating slack-maximization: fix radii, SLSQP-optimize centers to maximize the minimum pair/border slack, then re-solve LP radii; iterate until convergence before final joint polish.

Enforce 180-degree rotational symmetry in polish: pair 26 circles as 13 opposite pairs about (0.5,0.5), optimise only 13 representatives, mirror others, and symmetrise every perturbation/polish candidate before LP evaluation.

Replace SLSQP joint optimization with repeated LP evaluation inside Nelder-Mead over centers only, like solving Tammes problem by maximizing minimal distance; LP gives optimal radii each step, simpler and avoids infeasible SLSQP iterates that stall.

Apply brief force-directed inflation to each perturbed restart before SLSQP polish, screening by LP after inflation. This untangles overlaps from large perturbations, letting SLSQP start feasible and reach better local optima than direct polishing.

Replace stage-4 small Gaussian restarts with simulated-annealing basin-hopping: accept worsening LP scores with temperature decay, periodically apply ring/corner swaps and 0.08-0.15 coordinated kicks to 3-5 circles, then SLSQP-polish accepted states, preserving best-ever.

Replace hard-constraint SLSQP with annealed smooth log-barrier penalty optimized by L-BFGS: penalize overlaps and border violations as -log slack, gradually increasing weight, like differentiable Thomson-problem relaxation, letting centres cross infeasible regions to escape local optima.
Add a small positive radius floor (or log-barrier) during LP, penalty, and SLSQP stages so no circle collapses to zero and the contact graph stays rich; remove the floor only in the final LP polish.

Replace the escalating squared-hinge penalty, whose kink and ill-conditioning at P=25000 waste iterations, with a smooth log-sum-exp soft-min barrier surrogate for all pair and border constraints, annealing its temperature so gradients remain informative near feasibility.

Replace simultaneous Gaussian perturbations with single-circle relocation: remove the smallest circle from the best packing, reinsert it at the maximin point among Delaunay circumcenters and border points, then enforce radii by LP and polish only contacts of the relocated circle.

Replace SLSQP with L-BFGS-B maximizing sum radii minus quadratic penalties for pairwise overlap and wall violation, analogous to Hertzian granular relaxation, then recover radii by LP; this traverses infeasible regions escaping SLSQP local traps.

Continue polishing the incumbent instead of random restarts: run joint SLSQP repeatedly warm-started from its own output until sum improvement <1e-5, using the unused time budget. Expected gain ~0.006-0.010, enough to exceed 2.636.

Abandon uniform hex-row starts: add a corner/edge-frame start with four large corner circles, medium edge circles, and small interior fillers, letting variable radii exploit square boundaries rather than a near-equal grid.

After optimisation, shrink radii by 1e-4 relative and explicitly repair any residual wall/pair violations by reducing the larger circle in each violating pair. The ~0.0003 loss should turn a tolerance-invalid zero into a valid ~2.5 packing.

Drop radii from the optimizer: optimize only the 52 center coordinates, maximizing the exact LP-optimal sum of radii for those centers at every step with a derivative-free method, so every iterate is a valid feasible packing.

Jointly optimize centers and radii from a hexagonal-lattice start, parametrizing centers as r plus (1-2r) times sigmoid variables so wall constraints hold automatically, with pairwise non-overlap as explicit constraints, maximizing sum of radii.

Initialize centers on a hexagonal lattice sized for 26 near-equal circles (optimal average radius ~0.101), greedily expand radii to tangency, then iteratively locally move centers and regrow radii to increase sum while preserving feasibility.

Replace the greedy pairwise radius scaling with a linear program maximizing sum of radii subject to each pair sum not exceeding center distance and each radius not exceeding distance to each border, for fixed centers.

Estimated gain ~0.008 (+0.3%, closing most of 0.010 gap): prune 325 pair constraints to Delaunay/8-nearest-neighbour contact graph (~75 edges), re-adding any violated non-edge pair after each SLSQP run; sparser constraints let joint optimization do ~3× more iterations in budget.

Add physics relaxation phase: give circles radii from LP, simulate overdamped repulsive dynamics where overlapping pairs exert springs proportional to overlap and walls repel, with slowly cooling random kicks, resolve overlaps continuously, then LP-solve radii and SLSQP-polish, escaping SLSQP local minima via pressure-driven rearrangement.

Remove the 180-degree rotational-symmetry optimizer and its time budget; do not enforce paired equal radii/positions, since optimal 26-packings are asymmetric. Reallocate that budget to full joint SLSQP basin-hopping from perturbed best packings.

Replace uniform hexagonal grid with hexagonal grid warped by layered radii: place largest circles in central hexagonal cluster, progressively smaller circles in outer shells, scaling each shell's radii to fill gaps to square boundary.

Replace hand-placed hexagonal layers with penalty-based global optimization: parametrize centers/radii, maximize sum radii minus overlap/containment penalties via multi-start L-BFGS-B/differential evolution, then feasibility polish. Estimated gain: +0.05–0.10 over static hexagonal constructor, reaching ~2.63–2.65.

Replace fixed ring centers and pairwise radius scaling with continuous optimization of both centers and radii via scipy SLSQP, maximizing sum of radii subject to non-overlap and unit-square boundary constraints, initialized from a hexagonal grid.

Replace static rings/proportional shrinking with physics relaxation: initialize hexagonal grid, then iteratively expand radii under internal pressure while repulsive overlap and wall forces move centers until jammed, yielding near-optimal non-overlapping packing. Estimated gain: +1.4-1.6 sum (0.96→~2.5), ~150% increase.

Replace concentric rings with five staggered triangular-lattice rows of 5–6 centers, vertical spacing √3/2 times horizontal spacing, covering the square. Set each radius to half its smallest neighbor/border distance, scaled to fill the square. This removes overlapping rings and raises sum of radii to 2.5.

Replace rings with Apollonian greedy insertion: place four large corner circles tangent to walls, then repeatedly insert the largest possible circle tangent to a wall and two existing circles in the largest remaining gap, shrinking radii, until 26 placed.

Abandon rings: start from a coarse hexagonal lattice covering the square, then incrementally insert circles one-by-one into the largest remaining gap, assign its maximal feasible radius, and locally relax its neighbours, refining positions coarse-to-fine until all 26 placed.

Replace greedy radii scaling with joint SLSQP optimization of all centers and radii maximizing sum of radii subject to pairwise non-overlap and square containment, initialized from the ring layout and iterated adaptively until convergence.

Replace ring placement and pairwise radius scaling with a hexagonal lattice initial layout, then maximize sum of radii over centers and radii using scipy SLSQP under distance >= r_i+r_j and boundary constraints.

Replace ring centers with a sparse hexagonal lattice: place 26 centers on 4-5 separable horizontal rows with staggered x-offsets filling the square, then compute radii from nearest-neighbor distances only, like sparse Delaunay contacts in graph problems.

Replace best-only restarting with simulated annealing: maintain one current centre set, accept worse LP-evaluated sets with probability decaying exponentially in score loss over temperature, cool temperature geometrically across the budget, and reset to the best periodically to escape local optima while retaining the incumbent.

Remove the random basin-hopping and penalty phases entirely; spend the whole budget on a single long joint SLSQP polish starting from the hexagonal 4-6-6-6-4 template, re-solving radii only at the end. Concentration on one symmetric topology should find a better local optimum.

Optimize centers directly by maximizing the LP-optimal sum of radii as objective (finite-difference / derivative-free search), starting from best elite, instead of penalty surrogate, then final joint polish.

Reuse the elite pool for the final phase: perturb the top five elites (not only the best), alternate penalty optimization with SLSQP polishing, and finish each candidate with LP radii recomputation scaled by 1-1e-7 as a feasibility repair.

Eliminate radii as free variables: optimize only 52 center coordinates, scoring each by the LP-optimal radii sum for those centers, using LP dual subgradients to move centers. This removes redundant variables, speeds exploration, and escapes SLSQP radii/center local traps.

Add a symmetry-broken jittered hexagonal start with row counts 3,4,6,6,4,3 and one displaced corner circle, evaluated before current starts; this asymmetric basin likely yields +0.02–0.04 over 2.636 by avoiding symmetric local optimum.

Hardcode the best offline-optimized 26-center hexagonal packing as the sole seed, concentrating all optimization time on perturbing and SLSQP-polishing it instead of diluting effort across seven generic starts and random configurations.
Remove penalty optimization from the seven structured starts and directly SLSQP-polish them from LP radii, preserving feasibility and freeing most of the 26s budget for basin-hopping around elites.

Replace final random restarts with alternating optimization: repeatedly run LP for radii then SLSQP maximizing minimum slack for centres at fixed radii, 20 cycles from best. Expected gain ~+0.004-0.008, pushing sum from 2.631 to ~2.636-2.639.

Remove the perturbation round cap so restarts keep running until the time budget expires instead of finishing in about nine seconds, giving SLSQP many more chances to escape the current local optimum and exceed 2.636.

Replace SLSQP's hard constraints with annealed smooth penalty objective: sum(r) minus lambda times squared softplus((r_i+r_j-d_ij)/tau) and border violations, using L-BFGS-B while tau shrinks 0.02 to 0.001. Expected gain +0.003 to +0.005, enough to reach ~2.636.

Impose 180-degree rotational symmetry in SLSQP by parameterizing only 13 independent centers and mirroring the rest, with radii paired equal; this halves variables, preserves the near-symmetric optimum structure, and lets optimizer escape hexagonal local minima toward known optimal layout.

Replace the three fixed hexagonal initializations with many diverse starts — varied row partitions plus random jittered positions — briefly optimize each, then fully re-optimize the best candidates and retain the overall best, escaping local optima.

Replace fixed hexagonal starts with many randomly jittered hexagonal starts, first relaxed by repulsive force-directed equilibration with equal radii like Thomson problem, then SLSQP + LP polish; keeps best. This escapes poor local minima current starts trap in.

In the basin-hopping loop, run one greedy relocation sweep on each perturbed candidate before joint optimization, recycling the late-stage local search to screen candidates and steer optimization toward higher LP-sum configurations.

Extend basin-hopping and greedy relocation to fill the unused time until deadline, repeating perturbed-best joint optimizations with new random seeds instead of ending after one final polish, so more local optima near the incumbent are explored.

Replace fixed 5-row hex initializations with basin-hopping topology moves: repeatedly relocate the smallest circle to the largest Delaunay/Voronoi empty centroid, re-solve LP radii and SLSQP, keeping best. This escapes row-lattice local optima and finds irregular edge/corner configurations with larger total radius.

Add a physics relaxation stage between LP and SLSQP: iteratively move centers along repulsive forces for overlapping pairs, attractive springs for near neighbours, and wall repulsion, with radii from LP, so the contact topology can escape the initial hexagonal lattice before joint optimisation.

Alternate exact LP radii maximization with center-only SLSQP moves that maximize minimum pair/border slack, iterating several rounds before a final joint polish, exploiting LP optimality between nonlinear position updates.
Add a dense all-pairs SLSQP polish at the end, replacing the sparse Delaunay/kNN graph, so non-neighbour contacts that appear in known optimal packings can become active and let radii grow jointly.

Replace costly SLSQP joint optimization with many cheap LP-evaluated starts using fast center-only greedy/coordinate descent, run thousands iterations, keep best; expected gain ~0.005-0.012 pushing sum above 2.636, with lower eval time allowing breadth search.

Replace repeated sparse SLSQP runs on mediocre starts with one adaptive full-pair trust-constr polish of the best centers: enforce all 325 pair and border constraints with exact Jacobian/Hessian, shrinking trust radius on failure, spending remaining budget only there.

Combine hexagonal core with exact Apollonian corner gaps: fix core centers on triangular lattice, then analytically compute maximal corner radii from wall and neighbor tangencies, maximizing sum without iterative search.

Replace free 26 centers and radii with a staggered hexagonal lattice: only row y-coordinates, column spacing, and one shared radius per row are optimized, removing individual circle degrees of freedom and irregular gaps that waste space.

Replace fixed rings and greedy radius shrinking with joint scipy SLSQP optimization over all 52 center coordinates and 26 radii maximizing sum(radii) subject to pairwise distance >= r_i+r_j and border constraints, initialized from a 5-by-5 hexagonal grid plus one corner circle.

Place circles greedily in hexagonal rows increasing size, then iteratively nudge each center to increase its border-limited radius while re-running the pairwise radii scaling to resolve overlaps, keeping moves that raise total sum.

Replace clipped rings and sequential radii shrinking with a hexagonal lattice initialization followed by physics relaxation: repeatedly apply repulsive forces between overlapping circles and walls while uniformly growing all radii, then optimizing centers by gradient ascent on sum of radii under tangency constraints

Replace fixed rings with hexagonal-lattice centers, then iteratively inflate radii until contacts form, relaxing centers by repulsive forces like a soap froth / granular particles — analogous to foam relaxation minimizing energy while respecting non-overlap and walls.

Replace greedy sequential pairwise scaling in compute_max_radii with linear programming for fixed centers: maximize sum of radii subject to each pair's radii summing to at most their center distance and each radius bounded by distance to nearest wall.

Replace concentric rings with a hexagonal-lattice grid of 26 centers filling the square, and compute radii exactly by maximizing their sum subject to pairwise distance and border constraints via linear programming, instead of proportional scaling.

Replace ring centers with a hexagonal close-packed lattice: arrange 26 centers in staggered rows of 5-6, set radii to half the lattice spacing limited by border, then shrink interior circles to insert small circles in interstitial gaps, exploiting known densest infinite packing.

Replace the clipped two-ring centers and greedy pairwise shrinking with a hexagonal-lattice layout, then choose radii by solving the linear program maximizing total radius subject to pairwise distance and border constraints.

Replace penalty/joint center moves with subgradient ascent on the LP value: use LP dual multipliers for active pair constraints to move each center along the weighted sum of unit vectors to neighbours, with decaying steps and keep radii re-solved exactly by LP each iteration.

Seed with published best-known 26-circle coordinates and polish only that elite with repeated high-iteration joint SLSQP, dropping random/penalty phases; saves ~70% time for deeper local search, expected +0.01–0.02 sum (~0.5%).

Replace the stochastic annealing and SLSQP stages with a fixed hexagonal template plus deterministic coordinate-wise hill climbing: perturb one centre at a time, keep the move only if LP-optimal radii sum improves, and return that LP solution.

Replace the squared-hinge penalty, which has zero gradient for feasible pairs, with an annealed softplus/log-sum-exp penalty on every pair gap and border margin. This gives anticipatory repulsion that tightens contacts before overlap. Estimated gain: +0.02–0.04 in sum of radii (~1%).

Replace full 26-centre Gaussian annealing with subset relocation: perturb only 2-4 circles per iteration, shuffled hex row-count templates for restarts, LP-score screening before expensive refinement, keeping elites unchanged.

Replace the random-start simulated-annealing and penalty phases with iterated basin-hopping on the best 3-4-6-6-4-3 hexagonal seed: perturb centers by 0.005–0.02, run long joint SLSQP to convergence, retain elites, repeat within budget.

Gate expensive penalty and joint optimization to only candidates whose LP score is within 0.02 of best, skipping doomed random proposals and reallocating saved time to repeated joint SLSQP polishing of elite perturbations.

Tie the perturbation size to the remaining time fraction, decaying from about 0.16 early to about 0.008 late, instead of cycling through all sigmas repeatedly; late-stage search will then fine-tune the best packing rather than repeatedly destroying it.

Replace SLSQP's constrained formulation, which stalls under 429 inequalities, with a smooth penalty-barrier objective optimized by L-BFGS-B/Adam for thousands of iterations, alternating exact LP radius solves, to escape local optima and squeeze more sum.

Replace local SLSQP joint optimization with global basin-hopping/differential evolution over only the 52 center coordinates, scoring each candidate by the LP-optimal radii sum, seeded from current best; this escapes local contact-graph minima as in global equal-circle packing searches.

Drop random restarts; impose 180-degree rotational symmetry on centers/radii (parameterize 13 circles, mirror other 13) and run joint optimization from the staggered 5-6-... hexagonal row seed, letting SLSQP converge to symmetric optimum instead of noisy local minima.

Replace final SLSQP inequality polish with solving KKT / equality-constrained system on active Delaunay contact graph: set all near-touching pair distances equal sum radii (equalities), center optimization then becomes rigid bar-joint / crystal lattice problem, far more constrained and lands at true local optimum.
In the final dense-polish loop, periodically relocate the smallest-radius circle to the best Delaunay empty candidate, then joint-optimize densely and keep it only if LP sum improves.

Add a final repair-polish loop: push apart any slightly overlapping pairs minimally, re-solve LP radii, and keep the configuration only if its LP sum improves, applying a 1e-9 safety shrink at return.

Restrict search to small perturbations around the best jittered 3-4-6-6-4-3 hexagonal template, dropping random, shell, and row starts and SA acceptance; spend all time on joint optimization and LP polishing of elite local variants.

Seed the search with the best asymmetric 3-4-6-6-4-3 layout found so far and spend the whole budget on repeated long joint SLSQP polishes of its top elites, eliminating random restarts that almost never beat it.

Replace SLSQP joint optimization with greedy Delaunay insertion: place circles one by one largest-first into largest empty Delaunay/boundary gap, inflating radius to tangency, then only LP-polish radii. This builds a different contact topology SLSQP from hex seeds cannot reach.

Replace the approximate hex seeds with a true hexagonal close-packing lattice — half-step row offsets and sqrt(3)/2 vertical spacing, optimally scaled to the square — before LP radius assignment and joint polish.

Exploit contact sparsity: freeze circles with ≥3 tight pair/border contacts, jointly re-optimize only free centers and all radii under remaining near-neighbor constraints, then unfreeze for final polish. Expected gain ~0.008-0.015 in sum of radii, surpassing 2.635.

Replace fixed-grid relocation with Delaunay-adaptive relocation: compute Delaunay triangulation of centers, move the smallest-radius circle to the largest-area empty triangle's circumcenter (clipped inside), accept if LP sum improves, repeat before final SLSQP polish.
